reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; the unchanged paragraphs match the originals, so there is no invalid or directionally wrong edit to reject.

The rationale is supported by the cited text: the only amounts running from the Issuer/Depositor to Cellco are service-based compensation (Servicing Fee, Supplemental Servicing Fee), and no 'liquidated damages', penalty or minimum termination fee payable to the counterparty appears in the quoted paragraphs.

The two plausible candidates are correctly analysed and excluded under the rule's direction test: the $150,000 appointment fee and Additional Successor Servicer Fee (p0339, p0570) are compensation to a third-party Successor Servicer for services actually rendered (with transition expenses pushed onto the resigning/terminated Servicer under p0347, a term favourable to us), and the Make-Whole Payment (p0358) is yield maintenance to Noteholders on an Issuer-elected redemption, not a breach-triggered charge to the counterparty — and it is expressly excluded on a Clean-Up Redemption (p0351).

No deterministic checks failed, and retaining this as internal compliant evidence rather than a negotiation issue avoids over-flagging a securitization structure that does not impose Customer-payable liquidated damages.
